findings.evidence: The file provides `reorientHomEquiv_reorientKeep`, `reorientHomEquiv_reorientFlip`, both `symm` equations, `reorientHom_induction`, `reorientSymmetrify_obj`, `reorientSymmetrifyInv_obj`, four map equations for each orientation case, both inverse laws, and `reorientSymmetrify_map_reverse`; the docstring at lines 126–130 says exposure is only to support `rfl` proofs.
findings.fix: Remove `@[expose]` from lines 115, 121, 131, 192, and 206; retain the existing constructor/equivalence, object-map, arrow-map, inverse, and reversal lemmas as the public interface, proving their bodies internally with `:= (rfl)` where appropriate.
findings.issue: `reorientKeep`, `reorientFlip`, `reorientHomEquiv`, `reorientSymmetrify`, and `reorientSymmetrifyInv` are all marked `@[expose]` despite having public computation/elimination APIs; this exposes the sum encoding and prefunctor implementation to downstream consumers.

summary: Several public definitions expose their bodies even though the PR already supplies characteristic equations and eliminators, unnecessarily making downstream code depend on implementation details.
